title_en: Li Zhenghui v. Chai Guosheng — dispute over compensation for property damage
ruling_gist_en: Applying to the People's Court for preservation measures is a procedural right of the parties, but if the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for the losses caused by the preservation. The Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China does not prescribe how to determine whether a party's application is erroneous. To determine whether the applicant's application is erroneous, the specific facts of the case should be considered, including whether the applicant had fault in harming the respondent's lawful rights and interests through preservation, whether the preserved subject matter is the object of a dispute over ownership, whether the respondent suffered losses, and whether the preservation was for ensuring enforcement of the judgment. It is not appropriate to simply judge whether the applicant's application is erroneous based on the difference between the amount upheld by the judgment and the amount of property preserved.

full_text_en:
Li Zhenghui v. Chai Guosheng — dispute over compensation for property damage

【Ruling Summary】

Applying to a people's court for preservation measures is a procedural right of the parties to litigation, but if the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for the losses caused by the preservation. How to determine whether a party's application is erroneous is not provided for in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The determination of whether an applicant's application is erroneous should be made in conjunction with the specific circumstances of the case, by examining factors such as whether the applicant had fault in using preservation to harm the legitimate rights and interests of the respondent, whether the subject matter of preservation is a matter in dispute over ownership, whether the respondent suffered losses, and whether it was necessary to ensure the enforcement of the judgment. It is not appropriate to simply determine whether the applicant was erroneous based on the difference between the amount of claims supported by the judgment and the value of the preserved property.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2012) Min Shen Zi No. 1282

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Li Zhenghui, male, Han ethnicity, born on March 5, 1961, residing at Room 704, Building 2, Zone F, Dongyi Dongyi Garden, Guicheng Street, Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Guo Xianglong, lawyer from Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Wei, lawyer from Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chai Guosheng, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 12, 1953, residing at Room 1501, Building 7, Xiangzhang, Zhonghai Wanjin Haoyuan, No. 8 Jinyuan Road, Guicheng Street, Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhong Wei, lawyer from Guangdong Faze Ming Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Wanwen, lawyer from Beijing Dacheng (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

The Re-Applicant, Li Zhenghui, applied for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (2011) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 87 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of dispute over compensation for property damage with the Respondent, Chai Guosheng. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case. The examination has now been concluded.

Li Zhenghui applied for retrial on the following grounds:

(1) In the first instance of the other case (Supreme People's Court (2009) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 43, hereinafter "Case No. 43"), Chai Guosheng applied for preservation of 6,186,180 shares of Guangdong Cnlight Optoelectronics Science and Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Cnlight Company") held under Li Zhenghui's name (on the date of preservation, September 28, 2007, the closing price of Cnlight Company's stock was RMB 17.2 per share, approximately RMB 106.4 million) and two properties and one motor vehicle (valued at approximately RMB 2.2 million), with a total value of RMB 108.6 million. However, the court ultimately only supported Chai Guosheng's claim of RMB 23.74 million (the effective judgment ordered Li Zhenghui to return 348,259 shares of Cnlight Company to Chai Guosheng and to pay compensation of over RMB 19.29 million. On the date the judgment became effective, the stock price of Cnlight Company was RMB 12.77 per share). Chai Guosheng's excessive seizure application of RMB 84.86 million exceeded a reasonable scope and constituted preservation error. The judgment at first instance and on appeal failed to recognize Chai Guosheng's preservation error, which constitutes an error in the application of law.

(2) The Supreme People's Court case (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 572 (hereinafter "Case No. 572") is similar to the present case. According to the adjudicative viewpoint in that case, Chai Guosheng's excessive erroneous preservation in this case constitutes a tort.

(3) Chai Guosheng's erroneous application for preservation should bear the risk of depreciation of the subject matter during the preservation period. Chai Guosheng's application for preservation of the shares held by Li Zhenghui restricted Li Zhenghui's right to dispose of those shares. Under the principle of adaptation of rights and obligations, Chai Guosheng should bear the risk of value depreciation caused by stock price fluctuations. The price drop of Cnlight Company shares during the preservation period is a risk that Chai Guosheng should have foreseen and borne when applying for preservation. Chai Guosheng should be liable for compensation for such losses. This liability includes three aspects: first, the shares held by Li Zhenghui suffered depreciation losses during the lock-up period. Chai Guosheng should compensate for this part of the loss. Second, the loss in stock price after the shares held by Li Zhenghui became freely tradable, which should be calculated as the difference between the value on the date the lock-up expired and the value on the date the seizure was lifted. The judgment at first instance and on appeal found the relevant facts but failed to support this claim, which lacks a legal basis. Third, Chai Guosheng's preservation of Li Zhenghui's substantial property should compensate Li Zhenghui for the interest loss during that period. Chai Guosheng's seizure of Li Zhenghui's property restricted Li Zhenghui's right to dispose of it, resulting in Li Zhenghui being unable to use the preserved property for business activities. Therefore, ordering Chai Guosheng to compensate for the interest loss on the excessive portion of the preserved property during the preservation period is fair and reasonable.

(4) Chai Guosheng's erroneous preservation and failure to timely release the preservation caused Li Zhenghui to incur tax liabilities when disposing of the shares. Such taxes and fees should be borne by Chai Guosheng. The judgment at first instance and on appeal erred in failing to support this claim by Li Zhenghui.

In summary, Li Zhenghui requests a retrial of this case under Article 200, Item 6 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Chai Guosheng submitted a written defense, arguing that the application for preservation in Case No. 43 was in compliance with the law and did not constitute an erroneous application. Li Zhenghui's claim that Chai Guosheng's preservation application was erroneous has no factual or legal basis. The depreciation loss of the shares held by Li Zhenghui during the preservation period, as stated in his retrial application, simply does not exist, and there is no stock price interest loss. Li Zhenghui's calculation of his losses using the historical peak price of Cnlight Company shares during the lock-up period and his request for compensation from Chai Guosheng are baseless. Li Zhenghui's claim that he incurred additional personal income tax expenses because Chai Guosheng did not apply to the court in a timely manner to lift the seizure of the subject matter after the final judgment in the equity dispute case, and his request for Chai Guosheng to compensate for these losses, are groundless. Paying personal income tax in accordance with the law is a legal obligation of Li Zhenghui as a citizen. Therefore, Chai Guosheng requests that Li Zhenghui's application for retrial be dismissed.

This Court holds:

(1) Whether Chai Guosheng's application for preservation in Case No. 43 was erroneous.

Article 100, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where it may become difficult to enforce a judgment or cause other damage to a party due to the acts of one party or for other reasons, the people's court may, upon application of the other party, issue a ruling to preserve the property of the party, order it to perform certain acts, or prohibit it from performing certain acts. If no party applies, the people's court may, when necessary, issue a ruling to take preservation measures." Article 105 provides: "If the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for the losses caused by the preservation." According to these provisions, applying for preservation is a procedural right of the parties. However, if the exercise of this right is improper and causes property damage to others, compensation shall be made. In Case No. 43, Chai Guosheng filed the lawsuit because he believed that, under the agreement between the parties, the disputed shares should be fully returned if Li Zhenghui did not complete five years of service. To ensure the enforcement of a future judgment, he applied for preservation of the shares in question. This act itself was not illegal. Although the effective judgment did not support all of Chai Guosheng's claims, based on the evidence in the case, it is insufficient to find that Chai Guosheng had the intent or obvious negligence to damage Li Zhenghui's property through preservation. Furthermore, the purpose of the property preservation system is to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties and to ensure the enforcement of effective judgments rendered by the people's courts. Taking preservation measures necessarily prevents the preserved party from freely disposing of the preserved property in fact or in law. Therefore, simply judging that Chai Guosheng's preservation was erroneous because the amount of claims supported by the effective judgment was less than the value of the preserved property is inconsistent with the preservation system provided for in the Civil Procedure Law.

(2) Whether Chai Guosheng's preservation act caused stock losses to Li Zhenghui.

According to Articles 100 and 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, only when an applicant's preservation application is erroneous shall it compensate the respondent for the losses suffered as a result. Stock prices fluctuate. Based on the price fluctuations of Cnlight Company shares provided by both parties, although the price of Cnlight Company shares on the date of seizure, September 28, 2007, was RMB 17.2 per share, according to Article 142, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, which states: "The shares held by the promoter of a company shall not be transferred within one year from the date of establishment of the company. The shares issued before the public offering of shares by the company shall not be transferred within one year from the date of listing of the company's shares on a stock exchange," the initial public offering of Cnlight Company shares occurred on October 25, 2006. That is to say, the shares under Li Zhenghui's name could only be listed for trading as early as October 25, 2007. Even if Chai Guosheng had not applied for preservation measures, Li Zhenghui could not have liquidated his shares before October 16, 2007. Li Zhenghui resigned from Cnlight Company on August 28, 2007. According to Article 142, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law, which provides that "Directors, supervisors, and senior management of a company shall not transfer their shares held in the company within six months after their resignation," Li Zhenghui, as a senior management member of the company, could not transfer his shares before February 27, 2008. Based on the stock price movements from February 28, 2008, to February 22, 2010, the daily average closing price of Cnlight Company shares from February 27, 2008, to February 22, 2010, was RMB 8.41 per share. The closing price on November 4, 2008, was only RMB 3.75 per share. By the date of unsealing by the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, February 22, 2010, the closing price had risen to RMB 9.46 per share. If the stock price of RMB 3.75 per share on November 4, 2008, is used for calculation, after deducting the 348,259 shares to be returned to Chai Guosheng and the personal income tax payable upon the liquidation of the shares, the remaining stock value was essentially equal to the value of the stock preserved by Chai Guosheng. Li Zhenghui's calculation of his losses using the peak price of Cnlight Company shares and his request for compensation from Chai Guosheng are baseless and should not be supported by law. Due to the special nature of the stock market, its risks are unforeseeable. It is unreasonable to conclude that Chai Guosheng's application for preservation infringed upon Li Zhenghui's legitimate rights and interests based on stock price fluctuations. Furthermore, during the seizure period, Li Zhenghui did not propose to the court or to Chai Guosheng to trade or sell the preserved shares, nor did he apply to replace the seized items in accordance with the law.

After the expiry of the lock-up period for the shares held by Li Zhenghui, if he believes there was a loss during the seized period, there is an issue of how to calculate the loss. Analyzing the materials provided by both parties, during the period from February 28, 2008, to February 22, 2010, the highest closing price of Cnlight Company shares was RMB 15.33 per share, the lowest was RMB 3.75 per share, and the daily average closing price was RMB 8.41 per share, which was lower than the price on the date of unsealing. If one considers that the shares held by Li Zhenghui suffered losses during the seizure period, it is difficult to determine a base price for calculating those losses. Comparing the average price during the period from February 28, 2008, to February 22, 2010, with the price on February 22, 2010, Li Zhenghui did not suffer any loss. Subsequently, Li Zhenghui sold his shares and realized a total profit of RMB 84,357,958.45.

(3) Who should bear the tax loss.

In his application for retrial, Li Zhenghui also argued that after the judgment became effective, Chai Guosheng did not apply to the people's court in a timely manner to unseal the subject matter, resulting in increased personal income tax expenses for Li Zhenghui, which should be compensated by Chai Guosheng. On December 31, 2009, the Ministry of Finance, the State Administration of Taxation, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued the "Notice on Issues Concerning the Collection of Personal Income Tax on Income from the Transfer of Restricted Shares by Individuals Listed on the Stock Exchange," which stipulated that from January 1, 2010, personal income tax would be levied on income obtained from the transfer of restricted shares by individuals. Li Zhenghui signed for receipt of the second-instance judgment in Case No. 43 on September 4, 2009. He should have voluntarily performed his obligations in accordance with the content determined by the judgment. However, he did not actively perform, and he should bear the adverse legal consequences arising therefrom. Taxes are levied by the state and have no necessary connection with the act of applying for preservation. Li Zhenghui's claim in his retrial application that Chai Guosheng should compensate him for the additional personal income tax loss has no basis. The second-instance judgment in this case was correct in not supporting this claim.

(4) The relationship between this case and Case No. 572.

Although both Case No. 572 and the present case are disputes arising from the application for property preservation, there are significant differences between the two: First, whether the preserved party suffered losses. In Case No. 572, the subject matter of the preservation application was electronic products, among others, which are not suitable for preservation measures. In this case, the property preserved by Chai Guosheng was mainly shares of Cnlight Company. According to current market conditions, the prices of electronic products show a downward trend; stock prices fluctuate, rising and falling. The preserved party in Case No. 572 indeed suffered losses, whereas the preserved party in this case suffered no losses. Second, the fault of the preserved parties differs. In Case No. 572, both the preservation applicant, LG Philips Sunrise Electronics Co., Ltd., and the preserved party, Dongguan Peony TV Factory, were at fault for the losses of the preserved property. In this case, it is difficult to find that Chai Guosheng was at fault in applying for preservation. The dismissal of both parties' retrial applications in Case No. 572 was based on balancing the interests of both parties and the specific circumstances of that case, and it did not establish a standard for determining preservation error. In fact, the case with reference significance to this case is the Supreme People's Court case (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 271, which clearly states that applying for preservation of a subject matter with disputed ownership does not constitute preservation error.

In summary, Li Zhenghui's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided for in Article 200, Item 6 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. In accordance with the circumstances provided for in Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ordered as follows:

Li Zhenghui's application for retrial is dismissed.
